newsitem.title: USA: U.S. lowers shark quota, to close fishery to July.
newsitem.headline: U.S. lowers shark quota, to close fishery to July.

text.p: The U.S. Commerce Department said Wednesday it was cutting commercial shark fishing limits in half to 1,275 tonnes per year, and would close the commercial shark fishery from April 7 until July 1.

The rule, which will affect about 150 commercial fishermen, will remain in effect through 1997 "or until a more comprehensive shark rebuilding program is established and put in place," the Commerce Department said.
Under the rule, thousands of recreational fishermen will also be limited to catching two sharks per vessel on each trip and two Atlantic sharpnose sharks per person on each trip.

The fishery is being closed from April 7 at 2330 EDT through June because, with the new limits, fishermen have already met their quotas for the first half of the year. Each year is split into two seasonal quotas.
The rule bans direct fishing of five species of sharks considered to be very vulnerable to overfishing -- whale, basking, sand tiger, bigeye and white sharks.
It also sets a quota for first time for small coastal sharks.
The Center for Marine Conservation, which has pressed for limits on Atlantic shark fishing for years, welcomed the move, but said the population would take a long time to recover.
"Unfortunately, the serious depletion of these magnificent but vulnerable fish will take decades to repair," said the center's shark specialist, Sonja Fordham.
